chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn Abdullah, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), said:

I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you! Upon me is the fasting of a month if my uncle comes out of prison.' So he came out. I woke up in the morning intending to fast, and one of our companions came to me. So I called for the midday meal and ate with him. He said, 'There is no problem.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem/It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Does eating during the day invalidate a specific vowed fast if interrupted by a guest?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the ruling of a conditional vow (nadhr) to fast for a month upon a specific event, establishing its obligatory nature once the condition is met. It further provides practical jurisprudential guidance, confirming that breaking the fast for a necessary meal due to a companion's visit does not invalidate the vow, highlighting the flexibility within Shia fiqh regarding social obligations and vows.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Salih Bin Abdullah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! Upon me are Fasts for a month if my uncle would come out from the prison. So he came out. So I woke up in the morning and I intended the Fasting, and one of our companions came over to me. So I called for the lunch and had lunch with him’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Salih ibn ‘Abd Allah who has said the following: “I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, it is upon me to fast for one month if my uncle is released from jail. He came out from jail and I decided to fast the next day, but then a certain person of our people came and I invited him for lunch. I joined him for lunch. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful.’”
